items.summary: Upstream HKV: the TLPv2 and pointer insert kernels (tlp_v2_upsert/upsert_and_evict/find_or_insert, *_lock_key paths) skip LOCKED slots when choosing an eviction victim, so concurrent inserts into one full bucket can evict the second-lowest key while an in-flight insert holds the lowest score. hkv_adversarial_performance_benchmark (default quick mode) fails its exact top-128 admission oracle on MI300X in scenario bucket_skew_1over16 (12 to 556 oracle errors, timing dependent; tlp_v2_upsert_kernel_with_io). Same code path on CUDA; not run on an NVIDIA GPU to confirm. Needs a CUDA run, then an upstream report if it reproduces.

Upstream HKV: hkv_lookup_modes_benchmark with its default CMake parameters (capacity 134217728, kThroughput, bucket 128) inserts keys 0..100663295 at LF 0.75, which overflows 779 buckets (2661 keys must be evicted, computed on the CPU from the hash), so its 'membership_only failed successful-query check' (all queried keys found) cannot pass on any GPU. Seen on MI300X. An upstream benchmark issue, not a port defect.

Upstream HKV: dual-bucket (TableMode::kMemory) upsert hard-codes BUCKET_SIZE = 128 (dual_bucket_pipeline_upsert_kernel_with_io, Launch_DualBucket_Pipeline_Upsert, its SharedMemoryManager) and takes no bucket-capacity argument, while HashTable::init accepts any max_bucket_size in kMemory mode. A 64-slot dual-bucket table is therefore indexed as 128-slot buckets (out of bounds on every GPU). e10_dual_bucket_analysis (Part 2, bucket_size=64) hits hipErrorIllegalAddress / HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT in that kernel on MI300X. Fix belongs upstream (reject max_bucket_size != 128 in kMemory init, or parameterize the kernels).

Upstream HKV, every platform (source reading, not run): in tlp_v2_upsert_kernel_with_io (include/merlin/core_kernels/upsert.cuh, eviction loop 'if (min_pos < 0) continue;') a thread whose desired score equals MAX_SCORE (kCustomized with UINT64_MAX scores) spins while every slot of its full bucket is LOCKED; the holders are threads of the same block that publish only after the loop and after __syncthreads, so the kernel deadlocks on CUDA as well as HIP. The other TLPv2 kernels read keys(-1) on the same input instead (e.g. find_or_insert.cuh). Needs a CUDA reproduction, then an upstream report; not a port defect.

TheRock ROCm 10.2.0 (HIP 7.17.26434, rocm-systems pin 43fa692), Linux, gfx942: the same HIP runtime use-after-free already filed as ROCm/rocm-systems#14755 (LichtFeld-Studio deferral hip-event-query-destroyed-stream-uaf). hipEventRecord stores the recording stream in Event::captureStream_ on every record; hipEventQuery/hipEventSynchronize call checkEventCaptureRestrictions, which reads stream+0x234 (capture status) and locks stream+0x1d0 with no hip::isValid guard. HierarchicalKV's MemoryPool records its ready events on the caller's stream and queries them later from any thread; FindOrInsertPtrTest.test_find_or_insert_multi_threads destroys each worker's stream, so a later hipEventQuery in collect_pending_unsafe reads the freed hip::Stream and, when the heap has reused it, blocks forever in pthread_mutex_lock on a word no thread owns (__owner 0). The hang stack (libamdhip64 +0x1878f2 <- +0x1883f0 <- hipEventQuery+0x1b) is identical frame for frame to a 50-line reproducer that reuses the freed chunk (hangs 3/3 on 10.2.0, returns hipSuccess 3/3 zero-filled). Fixed on rocm-systems develop by #15025 (99ad350, merged 2026-11-18), not in 10.2.0; the reproducer passes 6/6 against the nightly 10.3.0a20261123 runtime (pin 51e17db, contains 99ad350). Nothing new to file: #14755 is open and the fix awaits a release. The port-side workaround is a person's ruling (notes.md, Porter 2026-11-24 round 3).

Remove the HIP-only event re-anchor in MemoryPool (include/merlin/memory_pool.cuh: event_stream_, the cudaStreamWaitEvent plus second cudaEventRecord in put_raw, its create in the constructor and destroy in the destructor; fork commit 4033ed6) once the minimum ROCm the port supports contains ROCm/rocm-systems#15025, the fix for ROCm/rocm-systems#14755 (hipEventQuery reads the destroyed recording stream). 10.2.0 does not contain it. Ruled by Jeff Daily 2026-11-24 (option a). When removing: drop the four #ifdef MERLIN_HIP blocks and rerun the 30-run test_find_or_insert_multi_threads loop on the new minimum ROCm.

gfx1201 (R9700, MES, num_cp_queues 4): two HIP processes on one GPU hang for good when each runs a one-thread kernel spinning on a device counter released by a kernel on another stream (HierarchicalKV group lock; 9 of 9 two-process pairs hang on two cards, 12 of 12 single-process runs pass; each process holds 5 compute queues against 4 slots). Killing the hung pair once left the GPU unusable for over 2 hours (new processes stall in their first packet). Issue draft for Jeff in notes ('Issue draft for Jeff', 2026-11-25), not posted; nearest existing report ROCm/rocm-systems#15850. A standalone reproducer has not hung yet. Port-side workaround drafted (fork commit 2fc61db, not pushed, untested).
